title: Knowledge check: Handling Missing Data

questions.prompt: For “Handling Missing Data”, which approach best supports a reliable result?
options: Inspect assumptions, run a small example, and verify an edge case.
Trust the first output without inspecting its inputs.
Hide warnings and skip validation to make the result look clean.
Change several unrelated parts at once so the cause of any result is unclear.
questions.answer_key: Inspect assumptions, run a small example, and verify an edge case.
questions.explanation: Missingness can be accidental or meaningful; deletion or imputation changes the analysis. Reliable work makes assumptions visible and checks behavior before scaling up.

questions.prompt: Which item is explicitly listed under “Handling Missing Data” in the source curriculum?
options: Change unrelated settings before checking the input
Assume one example proves every edge case
Skip validation when the output looks plausible
questions.explanation: The source PDF lists “Identifying Missing Values” as part of lesson 112. The lesson retains the original topic wording.

questions.prompt: When applying “Handling Missing Data” to real work, what should you do before relying on the result?
options: Validate inputs and output shape, test a boundary case, and state limitations.
Assume missing and malformed inputs never occur.
Use the same method regardless of data type or the research question.
Remove inconvenient observations without recording the decision.
questions.answer_key: Validate inputs and output shape, test a boundary case, and state limitations.
questions.explanation: Count missing cells first, state a handling rule, and compare row counts before and after. Record assumptions and known limitations instead of presenting a demonstration as proof.
